analysis.title: Dip buying lifts US stocks after tech slide (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: US stocks rose sharply on Monday 9 Nov 2026 as investors returned to tech and growth shares after last week's sell-off. The S&P 500 closed 2.4% higher and the Nasdaq gained 2.7%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 6.9%, while NVIDIA fell 4.3% after the start of an internal investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang. Most S&P 500 sectors advanced, with consumer discretionary and communication services among the strongest. Airlines and cruise operators gained on lower expected fuel costs.

Brent fell about 5.5% to USD 93 a barrel and WTI fell toward USD 87 as investors assessed potential progress in US-Iran diplomacy. Lower energy costs eased near-term inflation concerns ahead of Tuesday's US CPI report.

UBS reads Monday's rebound as dip buying and a reversal of some of last week's sharp derisking. The chip and AI infrastructure decline was amplified by elevated positioning, high expectations and uncertainty over data center development. UBS calls the sell-off a positioning reset, not the start of a lasting downturn in the AI investment cycle.

UBS says breadth of the rally is encouraging. Last week's weakness was concentrated in chips, data center companies and highly valued growth stocks, while Monday's gains spread across most sectors. UBS reads this as investors differentiating between companies and parts of the AI ecosystem rather than reassessing the growth and earnings outlook.

UBS says AI demand remains robust, citing accelerating cloud revenue and growing advance orders for computing capacity. It forecasts aggregate AI capital spending of USD 1.0tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. Political and physical constraints may delay, relocate or raise the cost of data center projects but are unlikely to eliminate demand.

UBS warns the rebound does not remove last week's risks. Investors increasingly want evidence that AI spending produces sustainable revenue, utilization and returns. UBS says further tech volatility would not be surprising.

Oil remains vulnerable after earlier supply disruption and inventory drawdowns. Diplomatic progress could push prices lower, while renewed attacks or a breakdown in negotiations could quickly reverse the move.

October CPI on Tuesday 10 Nov is the next test. Strong October employment data have kept expectations for a December Fed rate increase alive. A stronger-than-expected reading could lift bond yields and challenge the equity rebound. Contained price pressure would support a measured tightening cycle.

UBS sees gains in broad equity indices over the next 6 to 12 months on resilient earnings and growth. It suggests managing concentration risk, rebalancing across sectors and regions, and building a multi-asset core.

UBS prefers US industrials and health care, and the Eurozone, where it expects 2027 earnings growth similar to the US but with lower valuations. It favors established tech platforms with existing computing capacity, visible AI revenues, strong balance sheets and the ability to fund investment internally.

UBS suggests investors with large bond underweights rebuild strategic allocations in high quality short- and medium-term bonds. It says alternatives and broad commodity exposure can add return and hedge geopolitical or inflation shocks.
